title: What Leaders Do That Demotivates Talented Team Members
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Flips the usual motivation question, arguing that while what motivates people varies widely, what demotivates top performers is remarkably consistent. Identifies specific triggers: leader indecision that stalls progress, performative inclusion where input is solicited but ignored, over-control that strips autonomy, and coddling underperformers by holding everyone to the same standard. Warns that demotivated high performers often stay technically competent while quietly narrowing their effort and ambition, making the decline easy to miss until it's entrenched.
points: Leader indecision -- revisiting settled decisions, endless deliberation -- is one of the fastest ways to demotivate top talent.
Performative inclusion, where input is solicited but consistently ignored or reassigned credit, drives disengagement as much as outright exclusion does.
Demotivated high performers often remain technically competent while quietly narrowing their effort, making the decline easy for leaders to miss until it's entrenched.
quotes: Interestingly, while what motivates people is highly personal and can be very different from person to person, what demotivates them is generally consistent, especially for top performers.
When their leader revisits decisions already made, talks about the need to decide in endless meetings, or simply can’t choose, top talent will throw their hands in the air in exasperation.
When they find their proposals ignored, their suggestions quickly dismissed, their ideas credited to someone else, or their input solicited with no intention of the leader listening, they disengage.
Top talent takes particular umbrage when underperformers are treated the same as strong performers.
Because they are good enough to hide their dissatisfaction through minimal effort, demotivated talent often remains technically competent and productive to avoid performance flags.
Remember, leaders don’t crush the spirit of team members overnight. They do it one discouraging behavior at a time.
